assertion.name: Inebilizumab
assertion.description: CD19-directed cytolytic therapy is labeled for adults with AChR- or MuSK-antibody-positive generalized MG. MINT demonstrated overall MG-ADL benefit at week 26. The label describes the therapeutic mechanism as presumed; CD20 counts were used to assess B-cell depletion because the drug interferes with CD19 assays. Screen for HBV, tuberculosis and immunoglobulin deficiency, address vaccination and active infection, and monitor infusion reactions and immunoglobulins.

selected_evidence.snippet: UPLIZNA is indicated for the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adult patients who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) or anti-muscle specific tyrosine kinase (MuSK) antibody positive.

assertion.name: Thymectomy for Nonthymomatous AChR-Positive Generalized MG
assertion.description: MGTX randomized 126 adults aged 18–65 with AChR-positive generalized nonthymomatous MG of less than five years duration to extended transsternal thymectomy plus prednisone or prednisone alone. Surgery improved the three-year time-weighted QMG score and reduced steroid requirements. Older adults were included; age-subgroup analyses do not establish benefit exclusively in early-onset disease. Evidence for very old patients, long-standing disease, pure ocular disease, and other surgical approaches is less direct. MuSK-positive MG without a tumor is not an immunological indication.

selected_evidence.snippet: Thymectomy may be a potentially effective treatment for LOMG, particularly in patients who undergo the procedure soon after diagnosis. A randomized controlled study for LOMG patients is needed.

assertion.name: Rituximab
assertion.description: CD20-directed B-cell depletion is particularly supported for MuSK-positive MG. AChR-positive trial results depend on population and endpoint: BeatMG missed its primary steroid-sparing endpoint, whereas RINOMAX supported benefit in new-onset disease. Infusion, infection, and immunoglobulin risks require specialist monitoring; no efficacy ranking against other targeted drugs is inferred.

selected_evidence.snippet: Rituximab is a monoclonal chimeric Ab that specifically binds to the marker CD20 on the membrane of pre-B and mature B lymphocytes and causes transient B-cell depletion

assertion.name: Efgartigimod
assertion.description: Efgartigimod reduces IgG through FcRn blockade and has randomized evidence in AChR-positive generalized MG; seronegative disease is a separate trial question.

selected_evidence.snippet: Efgartigimod and rozanolixizumab are approved for AChR antibody–positive MG (128, 129), with the latter further approved for MuSK antibody–positive MG.

assertion.name: Azathioprine
assertion.description: A steroid-sparing immunosuppressant with delayed onset over months. Clinical and laboratory monitoring is necessary. Favorable outcomes in a late-onset observational cohort support applicability to older-onset patients but do not isolate a randomized combination effect.

selected_evidence.snippet: Due to the slow onset of action, therapeutic success with monotherapy is not to be expected before several months have elapsed.

assertion.name: Pyridostigmine
assertion.description: Acetylcholinesterase inhibition increases acetylcholine availability for symptomatic improvement without suppressing autoantibody production. MuSK-positive patients may respond poorly or tolerate it poorly; treatment is individualized.

selected_evidence.snippet: Patients with MuSK-Ab-positive MG may respond poorly to AChE-I and more often tolerate it poorly.

value.name: Tacrolimus
value.description: Tacrolimus is an alternative immunosuppressant. Two controlled trials did not confirm their steroid-sparing endpoints; post hoc score improvements provide more limited support.

assertion.description: Alternative broad immunotherapy; a selective antibody-production effect is not measured in the cited clinical synthesis.

selected_evidence.snippet: Other immunotherapies should be considered as second-choice treatment for MG with increased disease activity and can be used when contraindications, intolerance, or inadequate response to adequate doses of standard therapy apply.

assertion.name: Zilucoplan
assertion.description: A complement-inhibitory macrocyclic peptide for AChR-positive generalized MG. It binds C5 and also impedes C5b–C6 interaction. Its mechanism does not make it appropriate for the predominant IgG4 MuSK pathway. Meningococcal vaccination and infection precautions remain necessary; these agents do not directly stop autoantibody production.

value.name: Thiamine Repletion
value.description: Give thiamine promptly to prevent or treat deficiency-related neurologic injury. ASAM favors parenteral administration for poor nutrition, malabsorption or severe withdrawal complications. Prevention and treatment of suspected Wernicke encephalopathy require appropriate clinical protocols. Glucose can be given before, after or concurrently; urgent glucose should not be delayed while awaiting thiamine.

assertion.description: Replenishes a deficient vitamin to prevent or treat its complications; it does not directly treat reinforcement or craving.

selected_evidence.snippet: Thiamine should be provided to prevent Wernicke encephalopathy.

assertion.name: Disulfiram
assertion.description: An aldehyde-dehydrogenase inhibitor used as an aversive deterrent in selected patients pursuing abstinence. Informed agreement and support or observed dosing are important; drinking while taking it can cause a hazardous reaction. Supervised/open-label studies and blinded efficacy studies have different limitations. Avoid overstating comparative benefit from network estimates.
assertion.notes: Consider cardiac and hepatic contraindications and liver monitoring. It is not an anti-craving medication and requires informed patient agreement.

selected_evidence.snippet: Mechanistically, the medication inhibits the enzyme acetaldehyde dehydrogenase, which causes an accumulation of acetaldehyde.

assertion.name: Alcoholics Anonymous and Twelve-Step Facilitation
assertion.description: Offer peer support and, when consistent with patient preferences, structured professional facilitation of AA participation. In the 2020 Cochrane review, manualized TSF improved continuous abstinence at 12 months compared with other clinical approaches (two studies, 1936 participants; RR 1.21, 95% CI 1.03–1.42). Evidence for drinking intensity and consequences was less certain and generally did not show clear differences. These mostly US, noncoerced studies do not establish equal efficacy of every mutual-help format or an obligation to attend AA.
assertion.notes: The review found no measured quality-of-life or psychological-well-being outcomes. Proposed coping and social-network mechanisms and temporal mediation analyses do not demonstrate normalization of a specific brain circuit.

selected_evidence.snippet: If people with AUD are opposed to attending AA, despite the strong evidence for its potential to aid recovery, clinicians might consider linkage to alternative mutual‐help organizations as they may confer benefits at similar levels of engagement.

assertion.name: Acamprosate
assertion.description: First-line medication for an abstinence goal, generally started after withdrawal and abstinence. Trial evidence supports reduced return to any drinking, without a clear benefit for preventing return to heavy drinking. The molecular mechanism remains uncertain; it is not curated as a proven reversal of a particular glutamate abnormality. Severe renal impairment is a contraindication and moderate impairment requires dose adjustment.

selected_evidence.snippet: mechanism of action is unknown but likely modulates the GABAergic system.

assertion.name: Oral Naltrexone
assertion.description: First-line opioid-receptor antagonist for adults with moderate to severe AUD seeking abstinence or reduced drinking. Oral 50 mg/day has the strongest formulation-specific trial evidence for reducing return to heavy drinking; pair with appropriate psychosocial support and patient-defined goals. Current opioid use and acute hepatitis or liver failure are important contraindications; assess future opioid analgesia needs.
assertion.notes: Nausea, vomiting and dizziness can occur. Comparative trials did not establish universal superiority over acamprosate. Benefits concern consumption endpoints; evidence for mortality and other long-term health outcomes is limited.

selected_evidence.snippet: Naltrexone is a mu-opioid receptor antagonist that can be taken daily by mouth or as a monthly intramuscular injection administered in the clinic setting.

assertion.name: Topiramate
assertion.description: An off-label alternative when first-line medication is ineffective, contraindicated or not preferred. The Canadian guideline gives a strong recommendation with moderate-certainty evidence; systematic review supports reduced consumption endpoints. Cognitive slowing, language difficulties, paresthesias and other adverse effects require consideration. A 147-person 12-week comparison with naltrexone did not establish formal equivalence or superiority on its primary heavy-drinking outcome.

selected_evidence.snippet: Neither rs2832407 nor rs1799971 had effects on topiramate and naltrexone treatments, respectively.

assertion.name: Baclofen
assertion.description: A GABA-B agonist studied as an off-label option. The conventional systematic review found low-certainty evidence for preventing return to any drinking because results were inconsistent and imprecise; network ranking alone does not establish first-line status or broad safety. Sedation and tolerability require attention. ASAM finds insufficient evidence for treating alcohol withdrawal with baclofen.

selected_evidence.snippet: There is insufficient evidence to support the use of baclofen for the treatment of alcohol withdrawal.

assertion.name: Monitored Withdrawal and Level-of-Care Selection
assertion.description: Assess prior complicated withdrawal, current symptoms, medical/psychiatric illness and home support. Ambulatory care is for appropriately selected patients with reassessment; severe or complicated withdrawal requires an adequately monitored setting. Withdrawal management should connect directly to ongoing AUD care.

selected_evidence.snippet: Most withdrawal severity scales reflect current signs and symptoms and should not be used alone to determine level of care.

assertion.name: Benzodiazepine Withdrawal Management
assertion.description: First-line medication for moderate to severe alcohol withdrawal and prevention or treatment of withdrawal seizures and delirium, with monitoring for oversedation and respiratory depression. Symptom-triggered protocols require reliable assessment; fixed or front-loading approaches may be appropriate. Agent selection and dosing depend on liver function, comorbidity and setting. This is a short-course withdrawal treatment, not ongoing AUD pharmacotherapy.

selected_evidence.snippet: Benzodiazepines should not be prescribed as ongoing treatment for AUD

assertion.name: Long-term pancreatic and systemic follow-up
assertion.description: Follow type 1 disease for pancreatic or extrapancreatic relapse, exocrine and endocrine dysfunction, nutrition, bone health and treatment toxicity. Lifelong follow-up is advised by the European guideline, with frequency individualized to disease and treatment. Conflicting cancer-risk cohorts do not establish a proven AIP-specific cancer-imaging interval.

selected_evidence.snippet: However, these data might be inﬂu- enced by a bias due to a more careful surveillance of patients with IgG4-related disease or AIP. Thus, future prospective studies are required to analyse the inci- dence of cancer in patients with IgG4-related disease compared to age-, sex-, and risk factor-matched con- trol subjects.

assertion.name: Glucocorticoid induction for active type 1 disease
assertion.description: Glucocorticoids are first-line induction for symptomatic active type 1 AIP and selected patients with persistent mass, cholestasis or threatened organ function. Assess clinical, biochemical and imaging response after two to four weeks and taper individually. Glucose control, infection risk and bone health require attention. Treating every asymptomatic patient solely to prevent later pancreatic insufficiency is not supported; nonresponse requires reassessment of the diagnosis.

selected_evidence.snippet: There is no relevant data to support that a treatment should be proposed in patients with AIP without symptoms, just to limit the risk of exo- crine or endocrine insufﬁciencies. (GRADE 1C)

assertion.name: Rituximab for relapsing or treatment-intolerant type 1 disease
assertion.description: CD20-directed B-cell depletion is an option for resistant, relapsing or glucocorticoid-intolerant type 1 disease, or after failure of other immunosuppression. Most AIP-specific response estimates are from uncontrolled series. CD20-negative plasmablasts are not directly targeted; their decline is consistent with depletion of precursors. This is not a proven selective CTL therapy.

assertion.name: Inebilizumab for adult IgG4-related disease
assertion.description: The anti-CD19 antibody is approved in the United States for adult IgG4-related disease. In MITIGATE, 135 adults with active disease and a history of at least two involved organs received inebilizumab or placebo with the same eight-week glucocorticoid taper. Treated adjudicated flares occurred in 7/68 versus 40/67 over 52 weeks (hazard ratio 0.13, 95% CI 0.06–0.28). The trial was not a comparison with rituximab, did not establish pancreas-only efficacy, and does not apply to type 2 or checkpoint-inhibitor pancreatic injury. Serious adverse events occurred in 12 versus six participants and serious or opportunistic infections in six versus two. Screen for hepatitis B and tuberculosis, review vaccinations and immunoglobulins, and monitor infections and hypogammaglobulinemia according to the label.

selected_evidence.snippet: Monitor the levels of quantitative serum immunoglobulins during treatment with UPLIZNA, especially in patients with opportunistic or recurrent infections, and until B-cell repletion after discontinuation of therapy.

assertion.name: Mycophenolate mofetil as a steroid-sparing option

selected_evidence.snippet: Available data supporting the use of one agent over another are limited, but the use of azathioprine (2–2.5 mg/kg body weight) is generally recommended.

value.name: Glucocorticoids for symptomatic type 2 disease
value.description: Type 2 AIP usually responds to a short induction course followed by taper. Many patients do not require maintenance because relapse is uncommon in published series; associated IBD treatment and recurrence require individual assessment. Spontaneous improvement has also been reported.

assertion.description: Treatment reduces type 2 pancreatic inflammation; clinical response does not establish a specific neutrophil mediator.

selected_evidence.snippet: Type 2 AIP is a steroid-responsive disorder, and rapid improvements in symptoms and imaging abnormalities are expected within 2 or 3 weeks of the commencement of corticosteroids.6,7 Spontaneous regression without immunosuppression has also been documented. In contrast to type 1 AIP, in which relapse is relatively common (30% to 50%), disease relapse is uncommon in type 2 AIP (10%);6,7 therefore, maintenance therapy is unnecessary in most patients. The majority of patients with type 2 AIP present with features of acute pancreatitis (60%) or painless jaundice (30%).6,7 Episodes of acute pancreatitis in patients with type 2 AIP are clinically mild without the need for intensive care unit admission, the development of organ failure, or peripancreatic fluid collection.6 Other less common patterns of presentation include liver dysfunction, non-specific abdominal symptoms, and the incidental detection of a pancreatic mass on images taken for other purposes.

value.name: Diabetes management during pancreatic treatment
value.description: Assess and optimize glucose control before induction and during follow-up. Glucocorticoids can improve pancreatitis-associated dysfunction in some patients while causing or worsening hyperglycemia in others; pancreatic diabetes and pre-existing metabolic diabetes require individualized management.

assertion.description: Individualized diabetes care addresses hyperglycemia; it is not evidence that all pancreatic endocrine injury is reversible.

selected_evidence.snippet: Description The Japanese clinical guidelines recommend biliary drainage with biopsy or cytology in patients with obstructive jaundice, and control of blood glucose levels in patients with diabetes mellitus before steroid induction therapy [13].

assertion.name: Genetic counseling and family testing
assertion.description: Offer voluntary pre- and post-test counseling covering inheritance, variable penetrance, uncertain results, psychological implications and reproductive options. Test a known familial pathogenic variant when appropriate. Predictive testing for adult-onset disease in asymptomatic minors is generally deferred unless childhood actionability justifies it; symptomatic children warrant diagnostic evaluation.

assertion.name: Treatment of spasticity
assertion.description: Use physiotherapy and individualized antispasticity treatment when pyramidal symptoms impair function. Oral agents or selected focal botulinum treatment are symptomatic options; tolerability and effects on mobility guide decisions.

selected_evidence.snippet: Baclofen, tizanidine, or dantrolene may relieve muscle spasms & spasticity.

assertion.name: Physical rehabilitation and mobility support
assertion.description: Individualized balance, gait and strength training, mobility aids and fall-prevention adaptations support function. Goals and intensity depend on impairment and safety; rehabilitation is not established as a cure or proof of slowed molecular degeneration. A 62-person assessor-masked trial found greater SARA improvement with aerobic than dose-matched balance training; 43 participants had genetically confirmed SCA and the remainder had idiopathic ataxia or MSA-C. Selection required ambulatory function and safe cycling. This supports functional rehabilitation, not subtype-specific neuroprotection. In a separate uncontrolled seven-person SCA6/SCA31 cohort, annual intensive rehabilitation accompanied relative pre-session SARA stability through year six, while balance declined earlier; six-month follow-up SARA worsened from year three. Absence of a concurrent control prevents attributing long-term disease slowing to that regimen.

assertion.name: Hearing Intervention with Hearing Aid Provision
assertion.description: Audiological assessment, hearing-aid fitting, communication strategies and follow-up can improve audibility and communication. In ACHIEVE (977 adults aged 70–84), hearing intervention did not reduce three-year global cognitive decline overall. A prespecified recruitment-source analysis found less decline in the higher-risk ARIC subgroup, but not in healthier newly recruited volunteers; incident cognitive impairment was not significantly reduced. Hearing aids compensate for impairment and do not reverse its underlying cause.

value.name: Hair transplantation (follicular unit transplantation or extraction)
value.description: Follicular-unit transplantation or extraction redistributes donor hair to affected scalp and can improve coverage in appropriately selected patients. Adequate donor supply, realistic expectations and stable or medically controlled disease are important. Extraction avoids a linear donor incision but is not scar-free, and transplanted coverage does not prevent progression of native susceptible hair. The S3 guideline considers surgery in suitable men and women; combination medical therapy may help preserve non-transplanted hair.

assertion.description: Transplantation adds donor follicles to thinning areas rather than reversing miniaturization in the pre-existing affected follicles.

selected_evidence.snippet: FUE is a minimally invasive approach to hair transplantation that obviates the need for a linear donor incision.

assertion.name: Finasteride
assertion.description: Oral finasteride 1 mg daily inhibits type 2 5-alpha-reductase and is an established option for adult men with mild-to-moderate male-pattern hair loss. In two trials with 1,553 men during year one, target-area differences versus placebo were 107 hairs at one year and 138 at two years; these are between-group differences, not simple gains from baseline. Response may require 6–12 months and ongoing therapy. Counsel about sexual adverse effects and reduced PSA values. The 2025 EMA review confirms suicidal ideation as an adverse effect of finasteride tablets of unknown frequency and advises men taking 1 mg for hair loss to stop and seek advice if mood changes occur. Pregnancy exposure is contraindicated. The negative 1-mg postmenopausal-women trial does not exclude every female dose or subgroup.

selected_evidence.snippet: The frequency of the side effect is unknown, meaning that it is not possible to estimate it from available data.

assertion.description: Topical minoxidil is an established treatment for adult male- and female-pattern hair loss. The S3 guideline recommends 2–5% solution or 5% foam twice daily in men, and 2% solution twice daily or 5% foam once daily in women. assertion.description: A formulation-specific 24-week trial randomized 458 men aged 18–40 with mild-to-moderate vertex hair loss to topical finasteride 0.25% spray, placebo or oral finasteride 1 mg. Topical treatment improved target-area hair count versus placebo; the protocol-defined primary analysis included only 250 men with valid baseline and on-treatment photographs, although post hoc sensitivity analyses supported the direction of benefit. Numerical similarity to oral treatment does not establish efficacy equivalence. Low sexual-event counts and short follow-up do not establish superior long-term safety. Evidence for this specific spray should not be generalized to every compounded formulation or to women.

assertion.name: Statin Therapy
assertion.description: HMG-CoA reductase inhibition is foundational FH therapy. Response varies: selected D374Y carriers remained severely hypercholesterolemic despite treatment, while a small S127R series had substantial LDL-C lowering. These observations do not establish universal PCSK9-related statin resistance.
assertion.notes: FDA removed the blanket pregnancy contraindication in 2021. Most pregnant patients should stop statins; selected very-high-risk patients require individualized specialist assessment. Patients requiring ongoing statins should not breastfeed. The regulatory change does not prove fetal safety, and evidence about miscarriage remains insufficient. Preconception planning should address maternal risk and alternatives.

selected_evidence.snippet: Children: referral to a lipid specialist; diet and lifestyle modifications; statins can be used in children starting around age eight years.

assertion.description: Nonabsorbed bile acid sequestrant used as an adjunct for LDL-C reduction. It can be considered in pregnancy under specialist care; limited pregnancy experience and potential effects on fat-soluble vitamin absorption require consideration.
assertion.notes: The cited lipid-lowering studies concern broader heterozygous FH, not a PCSK9-specific treatment estimate. Pregnancy guidance is FH-wide and does not imply proven absence of risk.

assertion.name: Age- and Risk-Adapted Pediatric Lipid-Lowering Care
assertion.description: Treatment decisions use repeated lipid measurements, age, family history and other risks. IAS 2023 guidance recommends offering medication at ages 8–10 for persistent LDL-C above 190 mg/dL, with lower thresholds considered when additional risk is present. Drug selection follows local pediatric approvals and specialist assessment; these are broader FH recommendations, not PCSK9-specific trial thresholds.
assertion.notes: Long-term evidence for newer agents in children remains limited. Growth, adherence and adverse effects require follow-up. The cited age threshold is explicitly the 2023 IAS recommendation, not a universal regulatory label.

selected_evidence.snippet: Pharmacological treatment should be offered at age 8–10 years with an LDL-cholesterol concentration >4.9 mmol/l (>190 mg/dl), recorded on two occasions with a fasting lipid profile

assertion.name: Alirocumab
assertion.description: Monoclonal antibody against circulating PCSK9. A randomized placebo-phase study in 13 adults carrying D374Y, S127R, L108R or R218S demonstrated short-term LDL-C lowering on background therapy. Broader post-acute-coronary-syndrome trials support cardiovascular-event reduction in a different population.
assertion.notes: The 13-person trial tested a two-week randomized LDL-C contrast; its pooled eight-week 73.3% reduction had no concurrent placebo comparator. All participants received statins and six received ezetimibe. It was too small and short for cardiovascular-event or uncommon-safety conclusions. ODYSSEY OUTCOMES and ARCHITECT provide broader-population evidence; ARCHITECT was open-label and single-arm, without a reported PCSK9-stratified effect.

selected_evidence.snippet: Treatment with alirocumab in addition to high-intensity statin therapy resulted in significant regression of coronary plaque burden and plaque stabilization on coronary computed tomographic angiography over 78 weeks

assertion.name: Dupilumab
assertion.description: An IL-4R-alpha blocker used in eligible uncontrolled asthma/CRSwNP. In an open-label AERD cohort, 7 of 30 tolerated the highest aspirin challenge dose after six months and another 10 tolerated higher doses; this was not universal tolerance or a placebo-controlled comparison. Average polyp, asthma and smell outcomes improved. A nested 11-person 2026 mechanistic analysis found reduced nasal type 2 responses without a cytokine pattern reliably distinguishing tolerance; transcriptional associations do not establish mediation. NSAID use still requires individual specialist assessment.

assertion.description: Anti-IgE treatment may be selected under the applicable asthma/CRSwNP indication. A 16-person atopic AERD crossover trial reduced challenge-associated urinary LTE4 and allowed 10 participants to tolerate the highest tested aspirin dose after three months. assertion.name: Aspirin desensitization followed by maintenance aspirin
assertion.description: A specialist option for confirmed AERD with persistent symptoms, recurrent polyps or a separate need for aspirin. Benefits vary by patient and regimen: one 34-person randomized trial reported symptom/medication benefit, whereas a 2025 trial randomizing 26 successfully desensitized participants found no significant between-group difference in SNOT-22, asthma-control or polyp scores over 11 months. That trial used 125 mg daily initially then 250 mg and does not exclude benefit from other regimens. Screen for uncontrolled asthma, ulcer/bleeding risk, pregnancy and ability to adhere. Daily maintenance is needed; more than two missed days requires reassessment before unsupervised resumption.

value.name: Potassium Citrate
value.description: Alkalinising citrate is the treatment the 2025 ERA/ESPN recommendations place first for stone and nephrocalcinosis risk, on a weak recommendation grade because no human trial in Dent disease exists. The case rests on a high-citrate diet slowing CKD in Clcn5 knockout mice, on citrate's proven benefit in idiopathic hypercalciuria with hypocitraturia, and on citrate excretion in Dent disease being lower than in other Fanconi syndromes. Urinary pH needs monitoring, since over-alkalinisation risks calcium phosphate precipitation.
value.notes: Reported use is 13-25% of Dent disease patients. As citrate is metabolised to bicarbonate it also helps correct metabolic acidosis, but it may aggravate alkalosis in patients with significant hyperaldosteronism.

assertion.description: Citrate chelates urinary calcium and raises urinary pH, lowering the relative supersaturation that drives calcium crystal nucleation.

selected_evidence.snippet: Potassium citrate reduces recurrent calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis in patients with idiopathic hypercalciuria and hypocitraturia

assertion.name: Thiazide Diuretics

assertion.name: Concurrent male-partner antimicrobial treatment
assertion.description: Treating the woman's regular male partner with 7 days of oral metronidazole plus 2% clindamycin cream applied to penile skin, alongside her own first-line therapy. This is the only intervention here aimed at the reinfection route rather than at the woman's own vaginal community, and it is a reversal: six trials in the 1980s-90s were negative and guidelines do not recommend it, but the 2025 StepUp trial was stopped early because withholding it was inferior. Curated as a treatment because the trial result is randomised and positive, with the guideline lag recorded in the notes.
assertion.notes: Partner treatment was not recommended in guidelines at the time of the source review (PMID:34470644), which predates the StepUp result. The applicability of the trial is also bounded by its enrolment criterion - women in a monogamous relationship with a regular male partner - and should not be extended to other partnership contexts without evidence.

selected_evidence.snippet: Adverse events in treated men included nausea, headache, and metallic taste.

assertion.name: Tinidazole
assertion.description: A second-generation 5-nitroimidazole, FDA-approved for BV and a CDC-recommended alternative regimen, given orally as 1 g daily for 5 days or 2 g daily for 2 days.
